title: IBM releases an open 385M-parameter model for zero-shot time-series forecasting
friendlyTitle: IBM released an open model for forecasting demand, prices and other changing data
summary: IBM has released Granite Time Series PatchTST-FM-r2, a roughly 385 million-parameter model for forecasting demand, prices, energy loads, traffic and other time series without task-specific training. The weights, architecture, inference pipeline and benchmark code are available under commercial-friendly Apache 2.0 or OpenMDW 1.0 licensing.
friendlySummary: The model can make forecasts from time-based data without being trained again for every new dataset. IBM provides the model, code and a licence that allows business use.
whyItMatters: A compact, reproducible forecasting model gives businesses a testable alternative to maintaining a separate model for every dataset. Teams should compare it against simple statistical baselines on their own seasonal shifts, missing data and forecast horizons before deploying its predictions.
friendlyWhyItMatters: It may make forecasting easier and cheaper. Test it against a simple existing method on your own data before using its predictions for real decisions.
